title: Share a JavaScript property
summary: A property can accept a JavaScript value on an element.
introduction: A property can accept a JavaScript value on an element. Your task: Assign the points property a new number.
learningObjectives: Assign the points property a new number.
Explain the example for share a javascript property

blocks.text: A property can accept a JavaScript value on an element. A setter runs code when that property is assigned.
Run these HTML examples in this site's HTML playground. Each example defines its own custom element in a fresh page. No extra JavaScript library is needed.

blocks.code:
<point-display></point-display>
<script>
  class PointDisplay extends HTMLElement {
    set points(value) { this.textContent = "Points: " + Number(value); }
  }
  customElements.define("point-display", PointDisplay);
  document.querySelector("point-display").points = 7;
</script>
blocks.title: Share a JavaScript property

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`customElements.define` registers a hyphenated tag name with its class. Register a given name only once per document.
`querySelector` finds the first matching element. Check for a missing result when the element is optional.

blocks.text: The component shows Points: 7 after the property assignment.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A property and an attribute do not automatically update each other. Add that behaviour only when you need it.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Assign the points property a new number.
